summary: Add customer_note column, backfill all rows from note, create a sync trigger that keeps note and customer_note in sync, deploy the new staged version with state_only migration, retire the old version, then drop the note column.
write_consistency: A BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger on account_user sets both note and customer_note to COALESCE(NEW.note, NEW.customer_note), ensuring that writes from either version are reflected in the other column so concurrent traffic always sees the most recent value.
revision_notes: The previous plan's trigger only set customer_note via COALESCE(NEW.note, NEW.customer_note), which did not guarantee that new‑app writes to customer_note were visible to old‑app reads, and the backfill left some rows with only the note column populated, causing mismatches during the concurrent cutover. This revision adds a unified sync that updates both columns on every write, and backfills every row unconditionally so that customer_note is populated from the start.

stages.description: Add customer_note column, backfill all rows, and create a sync trigger.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT NULL;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION sync_note_customer_note() RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$ BEGIN NEW.note := COALESCE(NEW.note, NEW.customer_note); NEW.customer_note := COALESCE(NEW.note, NEW.customer_note); RETURN NEW; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
CREATE TRIGGER note_sync_trigger BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON account_user FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_note_customer_note();

stages.description: Deploy the new staged version; Django migration is state_only so the new version only knows the customer_note column.
Retire the old version; all traffic now goes to the new version which only reads/writes customer_note.
Remove the now-unused note column from the account_user table.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
